**Chapter 3: Structure of Matter**

**3.9 Atomic Mass or Relative Atomic Mass**

We already know that, the mass number of an element's atom is the summation of the number of protons and neutrons present in its nucleus. It certainly implies the idea that the mass number is an integer. But you will see the atomic mass of copper is 63.5 and the atomic mass of chlorine 35.5. How is that possible? Indeed, it is the relative atomic mass. What is it and why is it necessary?

The mass of an atom of Fluorine is 3.16×10^-23 g

The mass of an atom of Aluminium is 4.482×10^-23 g

It is really hard to use such small masses. That is why, 1/12 th of a Carbon 12 isotope is taken as a unit and then the atomic mass of other atoms are determined relative to that.

1/12 th atomic mass of Carbon 12 isotope is 1.66×10^-24 g

Therefore, the relative mass of the element:

| Name | Symbol | Proton Number | Mass Number | Neutron Number | A - Z |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hydrogen or Proteum | ¹H | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Deuterium | ²D | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| Tritium | ³T | 1 | 3 | 2 | 2 |

**[STIMULUS] What is the mass number of an element's atom?**

(a) The number of protons and neutrons present in its nucleus.

(b) The number of electrons present in its atom.

(c) The number of neutrons present in its nucleus.

(d) The number of protons present in its nucleus.

**[STIMULUS] What is the relative atomic mass?**

(a) The mass number of an element's atom.

(b) The mass of an atom of Fluorine.

(c) The mass of an atom of Aluminium.

(d) The mass of an atom of Carbon 12 isotope.

**[STIMULUS] Why is the relative atomic mass necessary?**

(a) Because it is the mass number of an element's atom.

(b) Because it is the mass of an atom of Fluorine.

(c) Because it is the mass of an atom of Aluminium.

(d) Because it is the mass of an atom of Carbon 12 isotope.
